title: Software Development Costs - ASC 985
learning_objectives: Distinguish internal use vs. for sale

two_types.software_for_sale_or_lease: Software developed to be sold or leased to customers (ASC 985-20)
two_types.internal_use_software: Software developed for company's own internal use (ASC 350-40)

activities: Coding and testing to establish technological feasibility

after_technological_feasibility.stop_capitalizing: When product available for general release to customers

technological_feasibility_determination.detail_program_design: Complete detail program design exists, confirmed to be achievable
technological_feasibility_determination.working_model: Working model completed and tested, confirms feasibility

includes: Payroll costs for employees directly involved

amortization_software_for_sale.method: Greater of: (1) Ratio of current revenues to total projected revenues (revenue-based), OR (2) Straight-line over economic life
amortization_software_for_sale.formula: Annual amortization = MAX[(Current revenue / Total projected revenue) × Capitalized cost, Capitalized cost / Economic life]
amortization_software_for_sale.economic_life: Estimated period product will generate revenue (typically short for software - 3-5 years)

amortization_internal_use.useful_life: Consider technological obsolescence (software often has short life - 3-7 years)

impairment.software_for_sale: Test when net realizable value (future revenues - costs to complete) < carrying amount. Write down to NRV.
impairment.internal_use: Test like long-lived assets when indicators present (two-step test per ASC 360)

calculation_example_for_sale.facts: Software project costs: $200K before technological feasibility (TF), $400K after TF until general release, $100K after release. Year 1 revenue $300K, total projected revenue $1.5M. Economic life 5 years.

entries.capitalize: DR Software Development Asset $400K, CR Cash/Accrued $400K
entries.amortize: DR Amortization Expense $80K, CR Software Development Asset $80K

calculation_example_internal_use.facts: Internal payroll system. Preliminary stage $50K, application development $300K, post-implementation $75K. Useful life 6 years.

entries.amortize: DR Amortization Expense $50K, CR Software Asset $50K

cloud_computing_arrangements.saas_arrangements: If customer does NOT take possession of software (SaaS), generally expense as service over contract term (not capitalized as software asset)
cloud_computing_arrangements.implementation_costs: Capitalize certain implementation costs in application development stage, amortize over contract term

website_development_costs.development_stage: Capitalize costs for graphics, content, software for operating website

cpa_exam_tips: Software for sale: Expense before technological feasibility, capitalize after until release
Internal use: Expense preliminary and post-implementation, capitalize application development
Amortization for sale: Greater of revenue-based or straight-line
Amortization internal use: Straight-line over useful life
Don't capitalize: Training, data conversion (unless required), maintenance, general overhead
Technological feasibility = key milestone for software to be sold

software_for_sale_timeline: START → Planning/Design → [TECHNOLOGICAL FEASIBILITY] → Coding/Testing → [GENERAL RELEASE] → Maintenance
capitalize_vs_expense_decision: 1. Identify software type (for sale or internal use)
3. For sale: Before TF = expense. After TF until release = capitalize. After release = expense.
4. Internal use: Preliminary = expense. Development = capitalize. Post-implementation = expense.
cpa_exam_strategies.amortization_approach_for_sale: Calculate BOTH revenue-based and straight-line. Use GREATER amount.
common_mistakes: Capitalizing costs before technological feasibility (should expense as R&D)
Using only straight-line for software to be sold (must compare to revenue-based and use greater)
Capitalizing preliminary stage for internal use (should expense)

key_points: Software for sale: Expense before technological feasibility, capitalize after until general release
Internal use: Expense preliminary and post-implementation, capitalize application development
Amortization for sale: Greater of revenue-based or straight-line
Amortization internal use: Straight-line over useful life
Technological feasibility = key milestone (detail design or working model)
Don't capitalize: Training, maintenance, general overhead, data conversion (unless required)
